name: Valacyclovir
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 1 g once daily (500 mg once daily if ≤9 recurrences/year)

common: Headache, nausea, abdominal pain (>10% in at least one indication, more than placebo)
serious: Acute renal failure (older adults; kidney disease with higher-than-recommended doses; other groups in label 5.2)
Central nervous system effects (agitation, hallucinations, confusion, delirium, seizures, encephalopathy)

contraindications: Clinically significant hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis, severe cutaneous reactions) to valacyclovir, acyclovir or any component
monitoring: Neurologic status in older adults and in kidney impairment

pk.half_life_eskd: Acyclovir about 14 hours in ESRD; about 4 hours during hemodialysis (label)
pk.metabolism: Rapid first-pass conversion to acyclovir and L-valine; no CYP450 involvement
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 46% of radioactivity in urine, 47% in feces (single 1 g dose)
pk.dialyzability: Yes: about one-third of body acyclovir removed in a 4-hour hemodialysis (label).

sources.citation: GlaxoSmithKline LLC. (2025). VALTREX (valacyclovir hydrochloride) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA020487, set ID f8e0d8f8-cb73-4206-a484-88f5c4fbd719, version effective November 12, 2025]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.
